html:
SMTO-CFG-0061 — SMTO doesn't recognize the shell access setting

GUID: ced4bbe5-ca4d-4f22-9ec6-efa514f43fbc
Slug: config-shell-mode-must-be-one-of-disabled
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • The shell access setting — which controls whether SMTO may run commands on a computer — has a value SMTO doesn't recognize, so SMTO refused it rather than guess how much access to allow.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you saw this on the Users page, select Manage for that user, choose an option under Shell access (or the Inherit option), and select Save user. That list offers only values SMTO understands, so saving replaces the unrecognized one.
  2. If SMTO stopped while starting, find AOR_SHELL_MODE where SMTO is started. Set it to disabled, read_only, approval_required or permissive, or delete it to use read_only. SMTO understands only these four values, spelled exactly like this.
  3. Choose the level you actually want. Permissive gives the most access, so pick it only if that's intended, not just to clear the error. This setting decides how freely SMTO can run commands, so a wrong choice could allow more than you meant.
  4. Start SMTO again from the same place where you changed the setting. The startup value is read only when SMTO starts.

What success looks like

  • The Users page shows Account updated, or the startup screen reaches Ready.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't change Unsafe actions or other permission settings to work around this error.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Settings validation rejected shell_mode (environment variable AOR_SHELL_MODE or a per-user shell_mode override) because after trimming and lowercasing it is not disabled, read_only, approval_required or permissive.

What this means

  • Effective shell_mode normalization yields a value outside disabled, read_only, approval_required and permissive. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • Effective shell_mode normalization yields a value outside disabled, read_only, approval_required and permissive.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the normalized effective mode and intended authority without switching to broader access merely to pass validation.

How to fix it

  • Set AOR_SHELL_MODE or the user's shell_mode override to exactly disabled, read_only, approval_required or permissive (when AOR_SHELL_MODE is unset, config.yaml runtime.shell_mode is used and is validated earlier under its own message; the default is read_only), then restart the Server or save the user again. Choose the mode that matches the intended authority; do not widen access just to pass validation.
  • Correct shell_mode to the intended supported authority mode.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The selected supported mode preserves the intended shell policy.

What not to do

  • Do not change an unrelated timeout, budget or policy. Check whether the named setting applies only to a new task.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
